title: De altitudine columnarum sub proprio pondere corruentium

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §35 of E510. Euler is looking for the critical parameter t at which a column buckles under its own weight. In the paper he has reduced the problem to power series P, P', Q, Q' in t. The critical t is the zero of the combination P(1+Q') − QP'. He tests the trial value t = 200: a positive value of the combination means t is too small, a negative one means it is too large. That is a sign test, the first step of trial-and-error or bisection root location.

Here he sums the alternating series P term by term using common logarithms. The recursion visible on the page is:
- log T_{n+1} = log T_n + log t − log r_n, with r_n = (3n−1)(3n)(3n+1)/(3n−2).
- The subtracted logarithms are those of 24, 52.5, 102.857, 171.6, 258.46, 363.375, 486.32, 627.27, 786.24 and 963.21, i.e. 2·3·4/1, 5·6·7/4, 8·9·10/7, and so on.
- So P = Σ (−1)^n t^n Π_{k≤n}(3k−2)/[(3k−1)(3k)(3k+1)]. This is a hypergeometric 0F2-type series of the kind that appears in the heavy-column equation, related to Bessel functions of order ±1/3.
- The companion series P' has terms T_n/(3n+2): 1/2, 1/5, 1/8, 1/11, 1/14, …, here 1/17, 1/20, 1/23, 1/26, 1/29, 1/32.
- Under each term Euler writes the running partial sum.
- Logarithms with negative characteristic are written in the 10-complement convention (lXI = 9,3267751 means log XI = −0.6732249).

The page carries both series from term V to term XI:
- P partial sums: 34.6288, −21.0427, 9.5987, −3.0027, 1.0152, −0.0068, 0.2054.
- P' partial sums: 2.3287, −0.9461, 0.5860, 0.0381, 0.1926, 0.1574, 0.1640.
- The next page converges these to about P ≈ 0.1734 and P' ≈ 0.1631, then starts on Q and Q'.
errors: No arithmetic errors found. Every logarithm sum and difference, every term value, every P' term (T_n/(3n+2)) and every partial sum on the page checks to the printed precision.
Minor numerical point: at t = 200 the terms reach about 72 before cancelling, so the 4-decimal partial sums lose relative accuracy. That is typical of alternating series and harmless for a sign test.

ideas.what: Summing an alternating power series for the buckling criterion by logarithmic recursion on the term ratio (3n−1)(3n)(3n+1)/(3n−2)
ideas.modern_name: Series solution of the heavy-column (Greenhill) equation, of 0F2 hypergeometric / Bessel J_{±1/3} type
ideas.usually_credited_to: Greenhill (1881) for the definitive heavy-column solution; Euler's 1778 attempts are discussed by Truesdell
ideas.where_published: E510 itself, with companion papers on columns (E508, E509); commented in Opera omnia II.11/II.10–11 by Truesdell

ideas.what: Sign test of a determinant-like combination P(1+Q') − QP' at trial values of t to bracket the critical load
ideas.modern_name: Root bracketing / bisection on the characteristic (secular) function of an eigenvalue problem

deep.surprise_reason: Pure numerical table: an arithmetically correct log-based summation of known series inside a paper whose content, the heavy-column problem, is already discussed in the history-of-elasticity literature (Truesdell). Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The page image shows the same values as the transcription. The label rows are mis-aligned: the 2,3010300 lines belong to the logarithm column, and the partial sums (+34,6288 etc.) sit under the term values in the P and P' columns.
The transcription's catchword 'lXI' at the page bottom is correct (the catchword is lXI).
